expected_finding: On the county's real payments, the many-to-one rule (R3) leaves the least money unexplained at each close and makes the most right calls on planted events; the one-to-one rules (R1, R2) cannot pair payments made of several invoice lines; R2's amount-and-date fallback pairs real payments that share an amount with the wrong bank line, so it hides some planted spurious debits; all three rules miss an invoice paid twice because every record agrees; a 5-day window flags most paper checks before they clear.
opposite: The county's amounts are distinct enough that the fallback makes no false matches, so R2 is as safe as R3 on the bank side; or R3's netting hides planted events that a one-to-one rule flags.

predictions.claim: R3 leaves less money unexplained than R1 and than R2 at every 2024 month-end close
predictions.opposite: R1 or R2 leaves less at some month end

predictions.claim: R1's mean unexplained money over 2024 closes is at least 2 times R3's
R2 makes at least 1 false match per 1,000 bank lines
R2 fails to flag at least 1 of the 40 instances of C1 and C6 through a false match
predictions.opposite: R2 flags all 40 or misses only without a false match

predictions.claim: each rule flags at most 2 of the 20 C4 instances (invoice paid twice)
R3 makes the right call on all 20 instances of each of C1, C3, C5, C6 and C8
at W = 5, at least half of Paper payments that cleared are a break at some close before clearing; the share falls under 10% only at W of 15 or more
R3 leaves less money unexplained than R1 and R2 at every month-end close, and R1's and R2's open items include every fee row older than W
predictions.opposite: R1 or R2 leaves less at some month end
